# Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.7 Launch (April 16, 2026)

Anthropic announced Claude Opus 4.7 on April 16, 2026, delivering substantial improvements across coding, vision, and agentic capabilities while keeping pricing unchanged.

## Coding and Benchmark Performance

The most notable improvements came in software engineering tasks. Opus 4.7 achieved **70% on CursorBench**, up from 58%, and scored **87.6% on SWE-bench Verified** [4]. It also posted a +10.9 point gain on SWE-bench Pro, reaching 64.3% compared to 53.4% for its predecessor [1]. Anthropic claimed the model solves 3x more production coding tasks than Opus 4.6 [5].

## Vision Capabilities

Vision performance saw dramatic improvement, with visual acuity jumping from 54.5% to 98.5% [5]. The model now supports images up to **3.75 megapixels**, three times the resolution supported by Opus 4.6 [1].

## Context Window and Technical Features

Opus 4.7 retained a **1 million token context window** with no long-context pricing premium, along with up to 128K output tokens [4]. New capabilities include file system-level memory and a new **xhigh reasoning tier**. Anthropic also introduced adaptive thinking via `thinking={"type": "adaptive"}`, replacing the previously supported manual extended thinking [1][4]. The model carries a knowledge cutoff of January 2026 [4].

## Breaking Changes for Developers

The launch introduced significant migration requirements. A new tokenizer uses **1.0–1.35x more tokens** for equivalent text, and parameters including temperature, top_p, and top_k were removed in favor of prompt-based behavior steering [1][4]. Anthropic warned that old prompts may break because the model now follows instructions more literally [1].

## Pricing and Availability

Pricing remained unchanged at **$5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens** [5]. The model was made available across Claude products, the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry [5].

One notable concession: Opus 4.7 showed regression on web search tasks, performing worse on the BrowseComp benchmark than its predecessor [1][3].
